ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit is a 5 V power supply, whose upper end is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to the middle upper node, and whose lower end is connected to the bottom common ground. The middle node connects downward to diode D1, and the lower end of D1 is grounded; judging from the symbol, the anode of D1 is at the top, and the cathode is at the bottom connected to ground. The right side of the middle node is also connected through another 1 kΩ resistor to the upper node on the right side, and this node connects downward to diode D2; below D2 is connected an 8 V power supply, and the other end of the power supply is connected to the bottom common ground. The polarity of the 8 V power supply on the right side makes the battery terminal connected to the lower end of D2 be -8 V relative to ground. Reasoning: According to the specified method, first assume D1 is open, and regard D2 as conducting. In this way, the middle upper node is connected through two 1 kΩ resistors respectively to +5 V and -8 V. The two resistors are equal, so the voltage of this node is the average of the voltages at the two ends: (+5 + (-8)) / 2 = -1.5 V. The cathode of D1 is grounded at 0 V, and the anode is -1.5 V; the anode potential is lower than the cathode, therefore ideal diode D1 is reverse-biased and cannot conduct. So the current in D1 is 0.0 mA.

method.method_draft: Inspect the image to determine source polarities and diode orientations. Treat D2 as conducting because its top terminal is above the -8 V battery terminal when connected through the resistors, and treat D1 initially as open. The two 1 kΩ resistors then connect the D1 top node between +5 V and -8 V, giving the node voltage -1.5 V. Compare this with ground at D1’s cathode: the anode is below the cathode, so D1 cannot conduct. Therefore the current in D1 is 0.0 mA.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For ideal diodes, a forward-biased diode is a short circuit and a reverse-biased diode is an open circuit. Since D1’s anode is at -1.5 V and its cathode is at 0 V, D1 is reverse-biased, so its current is zero.
